raw_case_text:
A 55-year-old previously healthy man presented with fever, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, myalgia, and dyspnea for three days after working in paddy fields. On admission, he was conscious, with low blood pressure (94/63 mmHg) and tachycardia (pulse rate 145 beats/min). There were bibasal lung crepitations, and urine output was only 10 mL over 4 hours. Admission blood tests indicated leucopenia and severe thrombocytopenia (Table 1).
After crystalloid fluid resuscitation noradrenaline was initiated to maintain blood pressure, intravenous ceftriaxone was commenced, and the patient was transferred to the medical intensive care unit (ICU). Due to severity of leptospirosis, intravenous methylprednisolone was administered for 3 days, and multiple platelet transfusions were given to correct thrombocytopenia. As oliguria persisted, intermittent hemodialysis was initiated. Dopamine was added due to persistent hypotension.
Chest radiograph indicated severe pulmonary hemorrhagic syndrome (Figure 1). Echocardiogram showed hypokinetic anterior wall motion and moderate mitral and tricuspid regurgitation. The patient was electively intubated and ventilated due to respiratory acidosis and hypoxia. Despite treatment, thrombocytopenia and abnormal liver function tests persisted (Table 1). Therapeutic plasma exchange was performed, and meropenem was commenced.
By Day 8, the patient was stable and afebrile, allowing for gradual withdrawal of inotropes. Leptospira microscopic agglutination test (MAT) became positive with a high titer. Blood picture showed low-grade hemolysis with a few red cell fragments.
On Day 21, the patient experienced fresh rectal bleeding. Upper gastroesophageal endoscopy revealed multiple gastric erosions, and colonoscopy revealed features of ischemic colitis. Blood and fresh frozen plasma were transfused, and intravenous proton pump inhibitor infusion was commenced. Exploratory laparotomy revealed extensive bowel necrosis from terminal ileum to the hepatic flexure with perforation and abscess formation of posterior wall of the ascending colon. Histopathology of affected areas confirmed these changes (Figure 2). There was no evidence of vasculitis in the rest of the peritoneal viscera. Standard right hemicolectomy and elective tracheostomy were performed.
On postoperative Day 1, the patient became unstable with hypotension and severe acidosis. Intact exteriorized bowel ends which had looked healthy at surgery showed features of ischemic necrosis. Since the patient's condition was unstable, further surgical exploration was abandoned. He succumbed on Day 27 of illness due to multiorgan failure.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 55-year-old man presented with a 3-day history of fever, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, myalgia, and dyspnea.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed acute fever, watery diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, myalgia, and shortness of breath 3 days prior to admission after working in paddy fields.
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously healthy man with recent occupational exposure to paddy fields.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, myalgia, dyspnea, and oliguria; later hospital course complicated by fresh rectal bleeding on day 21.

objective.physical_examination: On admission, conscious, hypotensive (BP 94/63 mmHg), and tachycardic (pulse 145 beats/min), with bibasal lung crepitations and severe oliguria (urine output 10 mL over 4 hours).
objective.routine_investigations: Admission labs demonstrated leukopenia, severe thrombocytopenia, impaired renal function, and abnormal liver function tests; peripheral blood smear showed low-grade hemolysis with occasional red cell fragments. Chest X-ray showed diffuse opacities consistent with severe pulmonary hemorrhagic syndrome. Transthoracic echocardiogram demonstrated anterior wall hypokinesis with moderate mitral and tricuspid regurgitation.
objective.advanced_workup: Day 21 upper GI endoscopy showed multiple gastric erosions, and colonoscopy demonstrated features of ischemic colitis. Exploratory laparotomy revealed extensive transmural bowel necrosis extending from the terminal ileum to the hepatic flexure with posterior ascending colon perforation and abscess formation; histopathology confirmed ischemic bowel necrosis without systemic mesenteric vasculitis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed severe leptospirosis complicated by pulmonary hemorrhagic syndrome, septic/cardiogenic shock, oliguric acute kidney injury, and fatal extensive ischemic enterocolitis, confirmed by high-titer positive Leptospira microscopic agglutination test (MAT). Treated in the ICU with crystalloid resuscitation, norepinephrine and dopamine infusions, IV ceftriaxone (later escalated to meropenem), IV methylprednisolone for 3 days, platelet/blood/FFP transfusions, intermittent hemodialysis, mechanical ventilation, and therapeutic plasma exchange. Although hemodynamically stabilized by day 8, he developed massive hematochezia on day 21 due to extensive ileocolonic necrosis and perforation, underwent right hemicolectomy and tracheostomy, developed recurrent stomal ischemia and refractory acidosis on postoperative day 1, and died of multiorgan failure on day 27 of illness.
